summary.title: Welcome to Shiny (Shiny tutorial, Lesson 1)
summary.one_liner: Learn how to install Shiny in R, understand the ui/server/shinyApp structure of an app.R file, and run and modify a first interactive histogram app.
takeaways: Install Shiny (and bslib) from R with install.packages(), then run the built-in Hello Shiny example with runExample("01_hello").
A Shiny app lives in an app.R file in its own directory, containing a ui object, a server function, and a call to shinyApp(ui, server).
Launch an app with runApp("directory"); press escape or the stop sign to end it and regain the R session.
Inputs such as sliderInput are read in the server via input$id, and renderPlot wraps output code so it re-runs when inputs change.
Hands-on exercise: change the app title, slider minimum, and histogram border color, then relaunch.
summary.summary: This is the first lesson of the official Shiny tutorial for R. It explains installing the shiny and bslib packages, then walks through the Hello Shiny example, which plots a histogram of R's faithful dataset controlled by a slider. It shows how an app.R file holds a ui object (layout via bslib's page_sidebar), a server function that uses renderPlot to produce reactive output, and a shinyApp call. Learners then create an app directory, run it with runApp, and make guided edits with model answers provided.
